review_notes: I read the whole file and the related definitions: `quotientMap_comp_mk`, `hankelIdeal_zero`, `hankelIdeal_one`, `constantCoeff_comp_quotientMap` and `rncMap_flat_iff`. I considered the repeated `hε` rewrites in `originDerivativeQuotient_mul` and `originIdeal_le_ker`. These are one-line calls to an existing lemma, so I did not report them. The `Q`, `phi` and `epsilon` boilerplate is also too small. The one real repetition is the argument that, when the Hankel ideal is ⊥, flatness of `quotientMap` and flatness of `rncMap` are equivalent through the bijective projection. It appears in `quotientMap_flat_one` and `quotientMap_not_flat_zero`. The gain is modest, and I have not compiled the proposed lemma.

findings.problem: Both boundary-degree proofs use the same reasoning. When `hankelIdeal R n = ⊥`, `Ideal.Quotient.mk` is bijective, so `Flat` for `quotientMap R n` is transferred to or from `Flat` for `rncMap R n`. Each proof rebuilds the bijectivity of the projection with `Ideal.Quotient.mk_bijective_iff_eq_bot` and `RingHom.Flat.of_bijective`. `quotientMap_flat_one` then builds a `RingEquiv` and proves a pointwise composition identity. `quotientMap_not_flat_zero` instead rewrites with `quotientMap_comp_mk`. The two directions of one equivalence are proved in two unrelated ways.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private lemma before both uses: `private theorem quotientMap_flat_iff_rncMap_flat_of_hankel_bot (R) [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (h : hankelIdeal R n = ⊥) : (quotientMap R n).toRingHom.Flat ↔ (rncMap R n).Flat`. For (→), set `hmk : (Ideal.Quotient.mk (hankelIdeal R n)).Flat := RingHom.Flat.of_bijective ((Ideal.Quotient.mk_bijective_iff_eq_bot _).mpr h)`, rewrite with `← quotientMap_comp_mk R n`, and apply `hmk.comp`. For (←), use the `RingEquiv.ofBijective` inverse `e.symm`, which is flat by `of_bijective`. Rewrite `quotientMap = rncMap ∘ e.symm` as in the existing `hcomposition`, then apply `.comp`. Then `quotientMap_flat_one R := (lemma R 1 (hankelIdeal_one R)).mpr ((rncMap_flat_iff R 1).mpr (Or.inl rfl))`. `quotientMap_not_flat_zero` becomes `fun h => ...` using `(lemma R 0 (hankelIdeal_zero R)).mp h`, followed by the existing case split on `rncMap_flat_iff R 0`. The hypotheses are the same: `Nontrivial R` is needed only in the zero case, after the lemma is applied, and the lemma needs neither it nor `Subsingleton R`.
findings.benefit: The bijective-projection transfer is stated and proved once as an iff, so the two boundary proofs reduce to short applications. A reader sees at once that degrees 0 and 1 differ only in the raw-map result they feed in. Any later change to the quotient/raw comparison is made in one place.

(quotientMap R n).toRingHom.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (hankelIdeal R n)) =
